title: Edit A Table Cell With Guards
task: Using docxedit only, inspect the document for a simple table cell that can be safely edited.
Create a .docxpatch using set-cell with expect-text and any useful row or column count guards you can infer.
Run docxedit check before apply and write the edited .docx under the run directory.
If every candidate table is complex or unsafe, stop after check attempts and report the relevant diagnostics.
Validate any successful output with docxedit read --max-text 0 and docxedit changes.
successCriteria: Uses stable table or cell IDs.
Uses at least one guard such as expect-text, expect-row-count, or expect-column-count.
Does not inspect raw OOXML package parts.
observerQuestions: Were table and cell IDs easy to discover?
Were guard fields clear enough for the agent to use without examples tailored to this document?
Did diagnostics distinguish complex table limits from syntax mistakes?
